title: 前联储主席直言：新掌门沉默，市场失去方向？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: We were all watching that news conference and it didn't start terribly and then progressively it just got more and more confusing. What was the point in that news conference where you sat up and
segments.zh: 我们都在观看那场新闻发布会，起初还算正常，但随后变得越来越令人困惑。在那场发布会上，从哪个时刻开始你坐直身子，觉得这不对劲？

segments.en: said this is weird. Well it's weird when you're not explaining why three people are dissenting yet the committee is deciding on no change in policy. There really was virtually no information
segments.zh: 嗯，当委员会决定维持政策不变，却不解释为何有三人持异议时，这就很奇怪了。实际上，几乎没有关于美联储如何思考货币政策的信息。

segments.en: about how the Federal Reserve is thinking about monetary policy, how the Federal Reserve is likely to react to incoming information in terms of how they adjust monetary policy. The silence of
segments.zh: 也没有关于美联储如何根据新信息调整政策的信息。沃什的沉默确实令人不安，金融市场基本给出了负面反应。

segments.en: wars was really quite toughening and the financial markets basically thumbs down. I mean the fact that the 30-year yield went up, the 10-year yield went up and two-year yields dropped really was a
segments.zh: 30年期收益率上升，10年期收益率上升，而两年期收益率下降，这确实表明那次新闻发布会失去了可信度。

segments.en: sign that there was a loss of credibility from that press conference. Bill, I want to highlight a distinction because I think it's important and it's in the body of your own pattern. I want to
segments.zh: 比尔，我想强调一个区别，因为我认为这很重要，而且它体现在你自己的模式中。我想替你说出来：你并不反对减少前瞻性指引。

segments.en: say it for you. You're not against reducing forward guidance. This is important. I think that the complaints about the people doing the complaining often are around the idea that somehow we still
segments.zh: 这很重要。我认为，那些抱怨的人往往认为我们仍然希望被牵着走，希望保留后流动性变化时代的沟通架构，但我认为你的批评并非如此。

segments.en: want our hands being held, that we want to hold on to the post-GFC communication architecture and but I don't think that's what your criticism is about. No I mean I wrote a group of 30 paper that
segments.zh: 不，我写了一篇三十人小组的论文，四月发表，其中一项建议就是取消前瞻性指引。只有在利率处于零下限、需要额外刺激时，才真正需要它。

segments.en: we published in April and one of the recommendations was to get rid of four guidance. The only time you really need four guidance is when you're at the zero lower bound for interest rates and you're
segments.zh: 但在其他时候，它只会束缚美联储，可能使美联储对信息反应更慢。

segments.en: trying to provide additional monetary policy stimulus. But the rest of the time it really just sort of inhibits the Fed and probably makes the Fed a little bit slower to react to incoming information.
segments.zh: 试图提供额外的货币政策刺激。但在其他时候，这实际上只是制约了美联储，可能使其对信息的反应更慢。
